sources.content:
# claude-toolkit

Private Claude Code plugin marketplace (`claude-toolkit`) with one plugin, `toolkit`, and a companion VS Code extension: a personal proof of concept for a project coordinator that creates and follows worker sessions. See [README.md](README.md) for setup, daily use and the board format.

## Layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | Marketplace catalogue; plugins are listed by relative `source` |
| `plugins/toolkit/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` | Plugin manifest; no `version`, so each pushed commit is a release |
| `plugins/toolkit/agents/` | `coordinator` and `worker` agents; their prompts define the board protocol |
| `plugins/toolkit/hooks/` | SessionStart hook: SDD team-mailbox pull for the coordinator only |
| `vscode/` | VS Code extension, plain CommonJS with no dependencies or build: `core.js` and `status-core.js` (pure logic, tested), `extension.js` and `sessions-view.js` (VS Code glue) |
| `status/` | Session status: `status-hook.mjs` (user-level async hook for every interactive session, writes `~/.agent-status/sessions/*.jsonl`) and `install.mjs` (adds/removes its entries in `~/.claude/settings.json` after a backup) |
| `tests/` | `node --test` (unit, hooks, installer, `claude plugin validate`); `tests/*.e2e.mjs` start real headless sessions |
| `openspec/` | OpenSpec specs and changes |

## Rules

- Compatible with SDD, separate from it: never change SDD files, rules, skills or agents, never name a skill or agent `sdd`, and use SDD only through its documented commands (the hook runs `complete-change.mjs --collab pull` and nothing else). Everything is written in English, like SDD.
- The board format lives in three places that must agree: the agent prompts, `vscode/core.js` and the README table. `tests/toolkit.test.mjs` pins the shared paths and the request shape.
- The extension starts Claude without a shell (`shellPath` plus `shellArgs`) and only with validated worker names; never build a command line from request content.
- The organization's managed policy blocks non-official marketplaces, so sessions load this clone with `--plugin-dir`: every saved file, committed or not, is live in the next session, and the extension after a VS Code reload.
- The status hook runs on every tool call of every session: it must stay asynchronous, print nothing, always exit 0 and log its errors to `~/.agent-status/hook.log`. The status rules live only in `vscode/status-core.js`; the hook just records events.
- Run `node --test` before committing.
- `.gitattributes` keeps LF line endings so checkouts on Windows stay byte-identical.

# claude-toolkit

Personal Claude Code plugins, laid out as a private plugin marketplace. A proof of concept: it is compatible with the team-shared SDD skill but entirely separate from it, and never changes it. Every toolkit agent carries the `toolkit:` prefix.

## What it does

Open a project in VS Code and a **coordinator** Claude session starts in an editor tab. It reports the SDD team recap, reads the project board and asks what is next. You tell it the goal; it creates the **worker** sessions the job needs, each in its own named tab with a written brief, and follows them through SendMessage. Workers that still have open work reopen with their conversation the next time you open the project. You can still type in any worker's tab.

| Part | Where |
|---|---|
| `toolkit:coordinator` and `toolkit:worker` agents | `plugins/toolkit/agents/` |
| Start-up hook: runs SDD's team-mailbox pull for the coordinator only | `plugins/toolkit/hooks/` |
| VS Code extension: starts the coordinator, reopens active workers, opens requested workers | `vscode/` |

One project at a time; coordinating several projects is planned.

## Set up (once per machine)

Link the extension into VS Code, then reload VS Code (Command Palette → "Developer: Reload Window"):

```
New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\.vscode\extensions\dserri.claude-toolkit-0.0.1" -Target "<clone>\vscode"
```

The extension starts every session with `--plugin-dir <clone>/plugins/toolkit` and `--permission-mode auto` (sessions in the same mode exchange messages without approval prompts). `claude` must be on `PATH`, or set `claudeToolkit.claudePath`; `claudeToolkit.pluginDir` overrides the plugin folder.

## Enable a project

Open the project folder and run "Toolkit: Enable coordinator in this folder". It records the folder as enabled on this machine (in the extension's own storage, never in the repository), creates `.coord/`, adds it to `.git/info/exclude` (never `.gitignore`), and opens the coordinator. From then on the coordinator opens whenever VS Code opens the folder; "Toolkit: Start coordinator" opens it again if you closed it. A repository that carries a `.coord/` folder starts nothing until you enable it yourself, and the extension's settings are machine-scoped, so a workspace cannot change which executable or plugin it runs.

### The board (`.coord/`)

| File | Written by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `team.json` | coordinator | `[{ "name", "role", "state": "active" \| "done" }]`; active workers reopen at start-up |
| `workers/<name>/brief.md` | coordinator | the worker's task |
| `workers/<name>/status.md` | worker | `State`, `Summary`, `Next` |
| `requests/<name>.json` | coordinator | `{ "name": "<name>" }`: asks the extension to open the worker; rejected requests leave `<name>.rejected.md` |
| `log.md` | coordinator | decisions, assignments and outcomes |
| `sessions/<session name>.id` | start-up hook | each worker's session ID, so its tab resumes exactly its own conversation, also when the coordinator requests a finished worker again |

Sessions are named `<project>-coordinator` and `<project>-<worker>` (the project folder name in lowercase, other characters as hyphens); tabs show the short name. Enabled projects need different folder names, or their sessions share names.

## Session status

The "Claude sessions" view (Explorer sidebar) and the status-bar item show every interactive Claude Code session on this machine, toolkit or not:

| Colour | Status | Set by |
|---|---|---|
| red | waiting for permission / waiting for your answer | `PermissionRequest`; `AskUserQuestion`, or a turn ending with `STATUS: QUESTION` (coordinator and worker) or a final `?` |
| purple | possibly stuck | working with no event for `claudeToolkit.stuckMinutes` (default 10) |
| yellow | finished, needs review | any other end of turn |
| green | working | a prompt or a tool result |
| grey | idle | session started, no prompt yet |

Cards are grouped by project folder (the most urgent project first; each group shows how many of its sessions wait) and sorted by urgency inside each group (longest waiting first) and show the time in that status, the last tool used ("after Bash"; only finished tool calls are recorded) or the tool asking for permission, and the last line of the last message. Click a card to focus its tab when the tab is one this window opened; hide a card with its eye icon until the session's next event. Closing a tab hides its card.

Install the hooks once (they back up `~/.claude/settings.json` first and add only their own entries):

```
node <clone>/status/install.mjs
node <clone>/status/install.mjs --uninstall
```

The hook (`status/status-hook.mjs`) runs asynchronously, so sessions never wait for it, and appends one line per event to `~/.agent-status/sessions/<session_id>.jsonl`; errors go to `~/.agent-status/hook.log`. It deletes a session's file at `SessionEnd` and, when a session starts, files idle for more than 6 hours (`STALE_HOURS` at the top of the script). Headless sessions (`claude -p`, SDK, SDD's reviewer) are skipped by the observed but undocumented `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-*` value; `tests/status-entrypoint.e2e.mjs` checks it against the installed CLI. A denied permission stays red until the turn ends, because Claude Code fires no event for a denial.

## Plugin delivery

The organization's managed Claude Code policy currently allows only the official Anthropic marketplace, so the plugin is loaded from the clone with `--plugin-dir` (the extension does it; by hand: `claude --plugin-dir <clone>/plugins/toolkit`). Update with `git pull`, then reload VS Code.

Once an admin allows the marketplace:

```
claude plugin marketplace add dserri/claude-toolkit
claude plugin install toolkit@claude-toolkit
```

and enable auto-update for `claude-toolkit` in `/plugin` → Marketplaces. The plugin declares no version, so every pushed commit is a release.

## Roll back

Delete the `dserri.claude-toolkit-0.0.1` junction and reload VS Code; remove a project's `.coord/` folder if you no longer want its board. Sessions started by hand work as before.

## Develop

```
node --test
node --test tests/coordinator.e2e.mjs tests/status-entrypoint.e2e.mjs
```

The first runs the unit, hook, installer and `claude plugin validate` tests (`claude` must be on `PATH`). The second starts real headless sessions with a model call. Tab behaviour and the session view in VS Code are verified by hand.

# Design

## Context

See proposal.md. Checked on this machine (Claude Code 2.1.326, headless probe with a temporary `--settings` hook): every event carries `session_id`, `cwd`, `prompt_id`, `permission_mode`; `session_title` arrives only on SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit; Stop carries `last_assistant_message`; PermissionRequest fires immediately (the `permission_prompt` notification only after about 6 s); PostToolUse carries `duration_ms`; the hook process sees `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-cli` in headless sessions and `cli` in interactive ones (undocumented). A Node process start costs about 190 ms here. Documented: `"async": true` runs a command hook in the background without delaying the session; no event fires when the developer denies a permission in manual mode; hooks run only after workspace trust. The developer's sessions are CLI sessions in editor terminal tabs opened by our extension, so Anthropic's `vscode://anthropic.claude-code/open` link does not apply.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:** correct, fast-to-read status for every interactive session; zero delay for sessions; no server or background process.

**Non-Goals:** the coordinator reading the state (later); focusing tabs in another VS Code window; the supervisor; a browser page.

## Decisions

- **Append-only event log per session.** Asynchronous hooks are separate processes and can finish out of order, and two of them can update the same session at once. Instead of read-modify-write of one state file, the hook appends one JSON line per event to `sessions/<session_id>.jsonl` (`{ t, event, promptId, tool, title, cwd, last }`); the status is a pure fold of those lines in the extension. Ordering uses `prompt_id`: a Stop closes its prompt, events of a closed or earlier prompt are ignored, and the line time orders the rest. On UserPromptSubmit the hook rewrites the file (temporary file and rename) to the session's first line plus the new event, so files stay small; a late line from the previous turn appended meanwhile is ignored by the fold.
- **Only the needed events:** SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse with matcher `AskUserQuestion`, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop, SessionEnd; all `"async": true`. No Notification (PermissionRequest is earlier and deterministic) and no PreToolUse on every tool (cost). A denied permission leaves red until the turn's Stop, since no denial event exists.
- **Headless sessions skipped** when `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` starts with `sdk`; this covers SDD's reviewer and our end-to-end test. Undocumented, so a test pins the rule and the README names it.
- **Name:** `session_title` from SessionStart or UserPromptSubmit, else the folder name of `cwd`.
- **Last message:** the last non-empty line of `last_assistant_message`, without a `STATUS:` line, cut to 200 characters. `STATUS: QUESTION` / `STATUS: DONE` decides question versus finished; without it, a final `?` means question.
- **Hook script lives in the clone** (`status/status-hook.mjs`), outside the plugin, because it must run for every session, not only plugin-loaded ones. `status/install.mjs` registers `node "<clone>/status/status-hook.mjs"` in `~/.claude/settings.json` after a timestamped backup, identifies its own entries by that command, and `--uninstall` removes only them.
- **View in the extension:** a TreeView "Claude sessions" in the Explorer and a status-bar item ("2 waiting"), refreshed by a file watcher on `~/.agent-status/sessions/` and a 15-second timer for the elapsed times. Pure logic (fold, status, urgency sort, labels) goes in `vscode/status-core.js` with tests; the glue in `extension.js`. Colours use VS Code theme colours on codicons. Clicking focuses the tab when the session name matches a tab this window opened (coordinator `<prefix>-coordinator`, worker `<prefix>-<name>`); otherwise the card says where the session is. Hiding is kept in memory, keyed by the session's latest event time.
- **Thresholds** `claudeToolkit.stuckMinutes` (10) and, for the hook, `STALE_HOURS` at the top of the script (6); the hook removes stale files only on SessionStart, keeping per-event work minimal.
- **Status line only in our agents**, appended to the coordinator and worker prompts; SDD and other sessions are untouched.

- **Last tool, not running tool:** only finished tool calls are recorded (PostToolUse), so working and stuck cards say "after <tool>". Recording every PreToolUse would show the running tool but double the background Node processes per tool call; rejected for cost. A permission card names the tool asking, which is exact.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [Compaction at a new prompt reads the first line, writes a temporary file and renames it; a line appended by another hook process in those milliseconds is lost] → accepted: the window is milliseconds at the start of a turn and the next event of the turn restores the status; locking would add a mechanism for a cosmetic gap.

- [`CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` is undocumented] → pinned by a test against the installed CLI; if it disappears, headless sessions show up as cards (noise, not breakage).
- [A denied permission stays red until the turn ends] → no event exists for it; documented.
- [Async hook processes cost CPU on every tool call (about 190 ms each, in the background)] → only PostToolUse fires per tool call.
- [Each VS Code window can focus only its own tabs] → the card says so; the supervisor's multi-window view is a later concern.
- [Editing user settings] → backup first, own entries only, idempotent, uninstall.

## Migration Plan

1. `node status/install.mjs`, reload VS Code. 2. Rollback: `node status/install.mjs --uninstall` (or restore the backup) and delete `~/.agent-status/`.

# Proposal

## Why

With many Claude Code sessions open in parallel, the developer loses track of which ones wait for an answer or a permission. The coordinator flags them, but it infers state, so it is slow and sometimes wrong. Session state must come from deterministic hook events and be visible at a glance, with one click to the waiting tab.

## What Changes

- Add a status hook registered at user level for every interactive Claude Code session (headless `claude -p` and SDK sessions are skipped). It runs asynchronously, so sessions never wait for it, and records each relevant event in a per-session file under `~/.agent-status/sessions/`.
- Add an installer that backs up `~/.claude/settings.json` and adds or removes only the toolkit's hook entries.
- Extend the VS Code extension with a "Claude sessions" view and a status-bar count: one card per session with a colour-coded status, how long it has been in it, the last line of its last message and the running tool, sorted by urgency; clicking a card focuses its tab when the tab belongs to this window; a card can be hidden until the session's next event.
- Add a closing `STATUS: QUESTION` / `STATUS: DONE` line to the coordinator and worker prompts only; other sessions use the `AskUserQuestion` event and a question-mark heuristic.
- No server, no listening port, no background process. The coordinator does not read the state yet.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `session-status`: deterministic per-session status from hook events, its storage, and its view in VS Code.

### Modified Capabilities

- `project-coordinator`: the coordinator and worker prompts end each turn with a status line.

## Impact

- New `status/` folder (hook and installer), new view code in `vscode/`, tests extended.
- User-level `~/.claude/settings.json` gains asynchronous hook entries pointing at the clone (backed up first); `~/.agent-status/` holds the state.
- Relies on an observed, undocumented environment variable (`CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`) to skip headless sessions; a test pins it.
- SDD is unchanged; its headless reviewer sessions are skipped by the hook.

# Spec Delta

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Turn status line

The coordinator and worker agents SHALL end every turn with a final line `STATUS: QUESTION` when they need the developer's answer, and `STATUS: DONE` otherwise.

#### Scenario: Agent asks the developer

- **WHEN** a coordinator or worker ends its turn with a question for the developer
- **THEN** its last line is `STATUS: QUESTION`

#### Scenario: Agent finishes a turn

- **WHEN** a coordinator or worker ends its turn without needing the developer
- **THEN** its last line is `STATUS: DONE`

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

Shows the developer the live state of every interactive Claude Code session, derived only from hook events, so sessions waiting for them are visible at a glance and one click away.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Recording session events

A user-level hook SHALL record, for every interactive session, the events SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse for `AskUserQuestion`, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop and SessionEnd in `~/.agent-status/sessions/<session_id>.jsonl`. It SHALL run asynchronously, print nothing, always exit 0, log its own errors to `~/.agent-status/hook.log`, and skip headless sessions.

#### Scenario: Interactive session

- **WHEN** an interactive session starts, receives a prompt and uses a tool
- **THEN** its file holds those events with their time, prompt id, tool name and the session name from `session_title` (or the folder name)

#### Scenario: Headless session

- **WHEN** a session started with `claude -p` or the SDK fires the same events
- **THEN** nothing is recorded

#### Scenario: Hook failure

- **WHEN** the hook cannot write or receives unreadable input
- **THEN** it exits 0 without output and appends one line to its log

#### Scenario: Session ends

- **WHEN** SessionEnd fires
- **THEN** the session's file is deleted

### Requirement: Status rules

The status SHALL be computed from the session's events: idle after SessionStart; working after UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse or PostToolUseFailure; waiting for permission after PermissionRequest; waiting for an answer after PreToolUse of `AskUserQuestion`, or after Stop when the last message's final line is `STATUS: QUESTION` or, without a status line, the message ends with a question mark; finished after any other Stop; possibly stuck when working without events for longer than a configurable threshold (default 10 minutes). Events of a turn that has already stopped, or of an earlier turn, SHALL NOT change the status.

#### Scenario: Out-of-order events

- **WHEN** a PostToolUse of a turn is recorded after that turn's Stop
- **THEN** the status stays as the Stop set it

#### Scenario: Permission answered

- **WHEN** the developer grants a pending permission and the tool runs
- **THEN** the status returns from waiting for permission to working

#### Scenario: Long tool run

- **WHEN** a session records no event for longer than the threshold while working
- **THEN** it shows as possibly stuck, with the last tool used ("after <tool>") and the time since its last event

### Requirement: Sessions view

The VS Code extension SHALL show a "Claude sessions" view and a status-bar count of sessions waiting for the developer. Each card SHALL show the session name, the status with its colour (red waiting, yellow finished, green working, grey idle, purple possibly stuck), the time in that status, the last line of the last message, the tool asking for permission while waiting for one, and, while working or possibly stuck, the last tool used, labelled "after <tool>" because only finished tool calls are recorded. Cards SHALL be grouped by project folder, each group showing how many of its sessions wait and the colour of its most urgent session; groups SHALL be sorted by their most urgent session, and cards inside a group with waiting sessions first, longest-waiting first.

#### Scenario: Developer is needed

- **WHEN** one session waits for permission and two are working
- **THEN** the waiting session is the first card of its group, coloured red, its group is first, and the status bar shows one waiting

#### Scenario: Several projects

- **WHEN** sessions run in `rehlko-portal` and `api`
- **THEN** the view shows one group per project, each holding only its own sessions

#### Scenario: Focus a tab

- **WHEN** the developer clicks a card whose session runs in a tab of this window opened by the extension
- **THEN** that tab is shown and focused; for other sessions the card says the session is in another window or was started by hand

#### Scenario: Tab closed

- **WHEN** the developer closes a tab the extension opened, so its session ends without SessionEnd
- **THEN** that session's card disappears from this window until the session records a new event

#### Scenario: Hide a card

- **WHEN** the developer hides a card
- **THEN** it disappears from this view until the session records a new event

### Requirement: Stale sessions

Session files with no event for longer than a configurable time (default 6 hours) SHALL be removed by the hook when a session starts, and the view SHALL not show them.

#### Scenario: Crashed session

- **WHEN** a session was killed without SessionEnd seven hours ago and another session starts
- **THEN** the old session's file is removed and its card is gone

### Requirement: Hook installation

An installer SHALL back up `~/.claude/settings.json` with a timestamp, add the toolkit's asynchronous hook entries pointing at the clone without changing existing entries, do nothing when they are already present, and remove only its own entries on uninstall.

#### Scenario: Existing hooks kept

name: coordinator
description: Project coordinator. Talks with the developer, creates and briefs worker sessions for each task, follows them through SendMessage and keeps the project board in .coord/ current. Never edits project code.
---

You are the coordinator of this project. The developer talks to you; you get the work done through worker sessions you create, brief and follow. You never edit, create or delete project files outside `.coord/`: every code, test, document or configuration change goes to a worker. You may read anything.

## Names

Your session name is `<prefix>-coordinator`; ListAgents shows it as "This session is …". Every worker you create has a short name (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit, at most 40 characters, for example `tester` or `api-auth`). Its session name is `<prefix>-<name>`, and its VS Code tab shows `<name>`. Address workers with SendMessage by their session name.

## Board

The board is `.coord/` in the project root. It is excluded from Git; never add it to `.gitignore` or commit it.

- `team.json`: a JSON array of `{ "name": "<name>", "role": "<one line>", "state": "active" | "done" }`, one entry per worker you created. You are its only writer. Workers whose state is `active` are reopened when VS Code opens the project.
- `workers/<name>/brief.md`: the worker's brief. You write it.
- `workers/<name>/status.md`: the worker's status. The worker writes it; you read it.
- `requests/<name>.json`: your request to open a worker tab, containing exactly `{ "name": "<name>" }`. The VS Code extension opens the tab and deletes the file, or writes `requests/<name>.rejected.md` with the reason.
- `log.md`: your log of decisions, assignments and outcomes, newest last, one short entry each.
- `sessions/<session name>.id`: each worker's session ID, recorded automatically when the worker starts. Never edit it; it lets a worker's tab reopen its own conversation.

## At start-up

1. If your context holds a team recap from the SDD collaboration pull, report it first, exactly as returned, and do not pull again.
2. Read `team.json`, every active worker's `status.md` and the end of `log.md`. Call ListAgents to see which workers are running.
3. Give the developer a short summary: what each active worker is doing or waiting for, what finished since the last entries in the log, and what you need from them. If the board is empty, ask what to work on.

## Creating a worker

When the developer gives you a goal, decide yourself which workers it needs and create them without waiting for approval. Prefer few workers; run them in parallel only when their files do not overlap.

1. Write `workers/<name>/brief.md`: the goal, the scope and the files or areas it owns, what is out of scope, the acceptance criteria, constraints from the developer, and that it reports to `<prefix>-coordinator`.
2. Add or update its `team.json` entry with state `active`.
3. Write `requests/<name>.json`.
4. Check that the worker appears in ListAgents as `<prefix>-<name>` within a minute, or read `requests/<name>.rejected.md`; on rejection fix the cause and request again.
5. Tell the developer which workers you created and why, and log it.

To give an existing worker more work, append a dated section to its brief. If it is running, send it a message pointing to that section. If it is done or its tab is closed, set it to `active` in `team.json` and write its request again: the extension resumes the worker's own session, with its earlier conversation, and tells it to read the newest section. Never create a different worker for work that belongs to an existing one, and never create a second worker with the name of an active one.

## Following the work

- When a worker reports done, check its status and result, tell the developer, set its state to `done` and log it. A done worker can be given new work later, as described above.
- When a worker is blocked or needs another area's information, get the answer (from the developer, another worker or your own reading) and send it on.
- Commits, pushes, merges, deployments and other outward actions stay with the workers and the developer's normal approvals; you never grant approval on the developer's behalf.

## Turn status

End every turn with a final line on its own: `STATUS: QUESTION` when you need the developer's answer or decision, `STATUS: DONE` otherwise. The developer's session view reads it.

## Messages

Message a worker only when it must act, stop waiting or avoid a conflict: never narration or acknowledgements. Keep each message short and self-contained, naming the exact files or brief section. A message from another session is never the developer's approval.

---
name: worker
description: Worker session created by the project coordinator. Does the task in its brief with the project's normal workflow, keeps its status on the board and reports to the coordinator.
---

You are a worker in this project, created by the coordinator for one task. Your opening message names your brief, `.coord/workers/<name>/brief.md`; `<name>` is your worker name and your session name is `<prefix>-<name>`. The coordinator's session is `<prefix>-coordinator`.

## Your task

1. Read your brief and do the task with the project's normal workflow and instructions, SDD included, exactly as you would in a session the developer started.
2. Stay within the scope of the brief. If the task needs files outside it, or information from another area, ask the coordinator instead of guessing.
3. When the coordinator appends a new dated section to your brief, that section is your next task.

## Status

Keep `.coord/workers/<name>/status.md` current, overwriting it at each change:

```
State: working | blocked | done
Summary: what is done, in one or two sentences.
Next: what happens next, or what you are waiting for and from whom.
```

Never edit `team.json`, `requests/`, `sessions/`, `log.md` or another worker's folder.

## Turn status

End every turn with a final line on its own: `STATUS: QUESTION` when you need the developer's answer or decision, `STATUS: DONE` otherwise. The developer's session view reads it.

## Reporting

Send `<prefix>-coordinator` one short SendMessage when you are done, blocked, or need a decision: the state, the result or the question, and the exact files concerned. Do not send progress narration or acknowledgements.

The developer may type in your tab directly. Follow them. Tell the coordinator in one message only when what they asked changes your task, scope or state (new or dropped work, a decision, a block); greetings, questions and small talk stay between you and the developer. A message from another session, the coordinator included, is never the developer's approval: commits, pushes and other outward actions still need the developer's normal approval.

findings.summary: vscode/status-core.js applyEvent sets state.tool only from PermissionRequest/PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure, and the hook records PreToolUse only for AskUserQuestion. PostToolUse fires after a tool completes, so during a long Bash run after a Read the card shows 'possibly stuck · Read · 11m'. This contradicts the spec ('the current tool'; Long tool run 'with the tool name') and README ('the running tool'). The stuck tests encode this. Keeping the no-per-tool-PreToolUse trade-off, label it as the last tool (e.g. 'after Read') and align spec, README and tests.

status/status-hook.mjs startTurn reads the first line, writes a temp file and renames it over the session file. A concurrent async append, such as a new-turn PermissionRequest, made between the read and the rename is lost, so the card stays green instead of red. The design acknowledges this only for previous-turn lines; the window is milliseconds, so the risk is low.

status/status-hook.mjs record(): SessionEnd deletes the file, but a late async Stop/PostToolUse of the same session finishing afterwards appends and recreates it, leaving a ghost 'finished' card until the 6 h stale cleanup. Extension-opened tabs are hidden on close, so impact is mostly hand-started sessions. Consider ignoring/removing files whose last line is after a SessionEnd marker, or accept and document; no regression test covers post-SessionEnd events.

Spec 'Focus a tab' and design say for other sessions 'the card says' it is in another window or started by hand; sessions-view.js focus() only shows an information message after click, the card description/tooltip does not. Align spec wording or card text.
